items.title: The stalk of the normalization at a point is the integral closure in the product of residue fields of the minimal primes of the local ring
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter morphisms.tex (Morphisms of Schemes)
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file morphisms.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma says that for a scheme whose quasi-compact opens have finitely many irreducible components, the stalk of the normalization's pushforward at a point is canonically the integral closure of the local ring in the total ring of fractions of its reduction, equivalently in the product of the residue fields of its minimal primes (statement lines 14465-14479). The counted proof is short but complete: it passes to an affine neighbourhood whose components all contain the point, identifies the stalk with an integral closure in a product of residue fields via the construction of the normalization, and then rewrites that product as the total ring of fractions of the reduced local ring, using that the minimal primes correspond to the generic points of the components through the point (proof lines 14481-14501). It is H2: the argument is carried out in the counted span, with the cited inputs being the construction of the normalization and the comparison of products of residue fields with total rings of fractions.
